topic: How PostgreSQL 17 incremental backups work (pg_basebackup --incremental, WAL summarization, pg_combinebackup) and their limitations

key_points.point: PostgreSQL 17 (released 2024-09-26) added incremental file-system backups via pg_basebackup --incremental plus the new pg_combinebackup tool and WAL summarization.

atoms.fact: PostgreSQL 17 added incremental file-system backups via pg_basebackup --incremental.
PostgreSQL 17 added the new pg_combinebackup tool.
PostgreSQL 17 added WAL summarization.
PostgreSQL 17 was released on 2024-09-26.

key_points.point: The server tracks changed blocks through WAL summary files, which record block numbers modified within an LSN range; they are produced by the WAL summarizer and kept under pg_wal/summaries.

atoms.fact: The PostgreSQL server tracks changed blocks through WAL summary files, which record block numbers modified within an LSN range.
PostgreSQL WAL summary files are produced by the WAL summarizer.
PostgreSQL WAL summary files are kept under pg_wal/summaries.

key_points.point: summarize_wal is off by default and must be enabled (it cannot run with wal_level=minimal); without it incremental backups cannot be taken.

atoms.fact: The PostgreSQL setting summarize_wal is off by default.
summarize_wal cannot run with wal_level=minimal.
summarize_wal must be enabled for PostgreSQL incremental backups; without it they cannot be taken.

key_points.point: wal_summary_keep_time defaults to 10 days; summaries must cover the whole LSN range since the prior backup or the incremental fails, so set it above the gap between dependent backups.

atoms.fact: The PostgreSQL setting wal_summary_keep_time defaults to 10 days.
WAL summaries must cover the whole LSN range since the prior backup, or the PostgreSQL incremental backup fails.
wal_summary_keep_time should be set above the gap between dependent backups.

key_points.point: pg_basebackup --incremental takes the backup_manifest of a prior backup from the same server; it uploads it, and the server sends only blocks changed since then (server version 17+ only).

atoms.fact: pg_basebackup --incremental takes the backup_manifest of a prior backup from the same server and uploads it.
For pg_basebackup --incremental, the server sends only the blocks changed since the prior backup.
pg_basebackup --incremental works only with server version 17 or later.

key_points.point: Incremental backups replace some relation files with incremental files holding only changed blocks plus reconstruction metadata; non-relation files are copied in full.

atoms.fact: Incremental backups replace some relation files with incremental files holding only changed blocks plus reconstruction metadata.
Non-relation files are copied in full in PostgreSQL incremental backups.

key_points.point: An incremental backup cannot be restored directly: pg_combinebackup must merge the full backup and all intermediate incrementals, listed oldest to newest, into a synthetic full backup with -o, then normal recovery follows.

atoms.fact: A PostgreSQL incremental backup cannot be restored directly.
pg_combinebackup must merge the full backup and all intermediate incrementals into a synthetic full backup (output directory given with -o).
The backups passed to pg_combinebackup must be listed oldest to newest.
After pg_combinebackup has produced the synthetic full backup, normal PostgreSQL recovery follows.

key_points.point: PostgreSQL does not track backup dependencies; deleting any backup in the chain makes later incrementals unrestorable, and pg_combinebackup validates chain relationships but not data integrity (use pg_verifybackup).

atoms.fact: PostgreSQL does not track dependencies between backups.
Deleting any backup in a PostgreSQL incremental chain makes later incrementals unrestorable.
pg_combinebackup validates chain relationships but not data integrity.
pg_verifybackup should be used to check the data integrity of backups, since pg_combinebackup does not.

key_points.point: pg_combinebackup does not recompute page checksums: if checksum state changed between backups in the chain, output may hold invalid checksums; take a new full backup after changing checksums.

atoms.fact: pg_combinebackup does not recompute page checksums.
If checksum state changed between backups in the chain, pg_combinebackup output may hold invalid checksums.
A new full backup should be taken after changing the PostgreSQL data-checksum state.

key_points.point: pg_combinebackup copies files by default (--copy); --clone (reflinks) and --copy-file-range can make reconstruction faster and save space where the OS and filesystem support them.

atoms.fact: pg_combinebackup copies files by default (--copy).
pg_combinebackup's --clone (reflinks) and --copy-file-range options can make reconstruction faster and save space where the OS and filesystem support them.

key_points.point: An incremental backup taken on a standby can fail if there was very little activity since the previous backup, because no new restartpoint may have been created.

atoms.fact: A PostgreSQL incremental backup taken on a standby can fail if there was very little activity since the previous backup.
An incremental backup on a low-activity PostgreSQL standby can fail because no new restartpoint may have been created since the previous backup.

key_points.point: Incremental backups mainly benefit large databases with mostly unchanged data; WAL archiving and recovery are still required, and for small or heavily modified databases full backups are simpler and similarly sized.

atoms.fact: PostgreSQL incremental backups mainly benefit large databases with mostly unchanged data.
WAL archiving and recovery are still required with PostgreSQL incremental backups.
For small or heavily modified PostgreSQL databases, full backups are simpler and similarly sized compared with incremental backups.

key_points.point: The output of pg_combinebackup is a synthetic full backup that can itself be used as input to a later pg_combinebackup run in place of the chain it was built from.

atoms.fact: The output of pg_combinebackup is a synthetic full backup that can itself be used as input to a later pg_combinebackup run in place of the chain it was built from.

key_points.point: PostgreSQL 18 added pg_combinebackup --link (-k), which hard-links files instead of copying them; input and output must be on the same filesystem, and changes to either side can affect the other.

atoms.fact: PostgreSQL 18 added pg_combinebackup --link (-k), which hard-links files instead of copying them.
With pg_combinebackup --link, input and output must be on the same filesystem.
With pg_combinebackup --link, changes to either side can affect the other.
